title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 1, QA) - Quant - Progressions
subject: Quant

questions.q: Suppose $x_1, x_2, x_3, \ldots, x_{100}$ are in arithmetic progression such that $x_5=-4$ and $2 x_6+2 x_9=x_{11}+x_{13}$. Then, $x_{100}$ equals
questions.explain: Let the first term be ${a}$ and common difference be ${d}$. $x_n = a+(n-1)d$. $x_5 = a+4d=-4$. The second condition is $2(a+5d)+2(a+8d) = (a+10d)+(a+12d)$, which simplifies to $4a+26d=2a+22d$, giving $2a=-4d$ or $a=-2d$. Substitute this into the first condition: $(-2d)+4d=-4 \Rightarrow 2d=-4 \Rightarrow d=-2$. Then $a=4$. We want $x_{100} = a+99d = 4+99(-2)=4-198=-194$.
